newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 3.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

West Indian batsman Brian Lara has scored his first century of the test match series against Australia at the WACA ground in Perth. Lara and opening batsman Robert Samuels helped the West Indies to 7 wickets for 353, a 110 run first innings lead. Australin bowler Paul Reiffel took three wickets, while Shane Warne and Glenn McGrath had two each. Page 25.

Australian skiff sailors David Witt and Michael Spies are expected to announce a challenge for the Whitbread around the world yacht race this week with the signing of a major sponsor on Thursday. Witt and Spies have been working on their project for more han four months and have selected half their team for the race starting in England in September. Page 26.

The Australian Open may be moved from January to March following searing heat conditions at this year's event. Tennis Australia is considering playing the Open a week later than usual or in March. Players complained of the heat at this year's open and officals closed the centre court roof due to the conditions. Page 29.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian world champion time-trial cyclist Shane Kelly is competing in the summer track-cycling program in Australia for the first time in five years instead of pre-season altitude training overseas. Kelly won the Holeproof and Repco Cyclists Internatioal Cup on Saturday night at the Northcote Velodrome in Melbourne. Page 26.

Australian triathlete Greg Welch won round two of the St George Bank Triathlon series in Glenelg yesterday. World champion Brad Bevan still leads the series after finishing third, while Jackie Gallagher won the women's race. Page 27.

Australian swimmer Matthew Dunn finished second in the World Cup 400m individual medley in Gelsenkirchen, Germany, on Saturday but still broke a world shortcourse record. Dutch rival Marcel Wouda finished at 4min 05.59s, three-hundredths of a second ahead of Dunn. Page 29.
THE AGE

Spain's Miguel Angel Martin won the Heineken Classic at the Vines in Perth yesterday. Martin birdied the 18th hole to win with a total 15 under par 273, a one shot victory over American Fred Couples. Page 2.

Victoria defeated New South Wales in their Sheffield Shield cricket match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground last night by making its largest fourth innings run chase in 65 years. After collapsing in their first innings, Victoria made 391 runs, with Graeme Vimpani making 161. The win puts Victoria in contention for second place on the shield table. Page 5.

Australian Football League veterans Greg Williams and Justin Madden will almost certainly play one more season for their club, Carlton. Thirty-three-year-old Williams and 35 year-old Madden are out of contract and will need to negotiate one-year deals with the club. Page 2.
THE HERALD SUN

Australia was beaten 12-10 by New Zealand in the rugby league World Nines tournament in Townsville yesterday. New Zealand then went on to defeat Western Samoa 16-0 in the final. Australia was odds-on favourite for the super-league title, and will play New Zealand again in an Anzac Day test match. Page 72. --

Former Australian road cycling champion Alan Iacuone won the 800km Tour of Tasmania yesterday. Iacuone broke away on Saturday from overnight leader Peter Rogers to take an unbeatable 17 minute lead. Page 72.

Australian sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor will compete against young rival Lauren Hewitt in Paris next month. Taylor and Hewitt are part of a seven-strong Australian team competing at the March 7-9 championships. Gainsford-Taylor is the defending 200 metre indoor champion at Paris. Page 69.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian sailor Chris Nicholson is overall winner of the Oracle Grand Prix 18 footer series. The defending champion, Nicholson came from behind in the final event of the series to win on Sydney Harbour. Nicholson is Australia's gold medal sailing hope in the year 2000 Sydney Olympics. Page 29.

Victorian Hamish Cameron won the annual Bondi Beach Cole Classic two kilometre ocean swimming race yesterday from defending champion Kurt Eldridge and Australian Olympic swimmer Malcolm Allen. Olympian Stacy Gartrell defended her title in the race. Page 3.
Perth Glory kept on track for the playoffs of the Ericsson soccer Cup by defeating UTS Olympic at Belmore Sports Ground last night. The Glory took a 2-0 half-time score to win the match. Page 33.
(Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
